hints: Focus on the carbocation formed when $H^+$ adds to the double bond, since its stability controls the speed.
Work out the intermediate from each alkene: ethene gives a primary cation, propene gives a secondary cation, and 2-methylpropene gives a tertiary cation.
Remember the stability order tertiary > secondary > primary, then list the alkenes from slowest (least stable) to fastest (most stable).
walkthrough:
**Link speed to carbocation stability**

Think of it like this, a more comfortable intermediate means a lower activation energy and a faster reaction. Here we are told directly: more stable carbocation = faster reaction.

Rule to use:
$$\text{tertiary} > \text{secondary} > \text{primary in stability and speed}$$

**Draw the intermediate from each alkene**

Add $H^+$ to the $C=C$ bond to make the most stable carbocation (Markovnikov addition).

$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2 + H^+ \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2^+ \text{ (primary)}$$ 
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + H^+ \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}^+\text{CH}_3 \text{ (secondary)}$$ 
$$\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C}=\text{CH}_2 + H^+ \rightarrow \text{(CH}_3\text{)}_3\text{C}^+ \text{ (tertiary)}$$

**Rank by alkyl groups and inductive effect**

Alkyl groups push electron density toward the positive carbon and spread the charge. More alkyl groups attached means more stable.

So ethene (0 extra alkyl on cation carbon beyond one) is slowest, propene is in the middle, and 2-methylpropene is fastest.

**Write the increasing speed sequence**

Increasing means slowest first and fastest last.

$$\text{ethene < propene < 2-methylpropene}$$

options.A: Correct. Ethene forms a primary carbocation, propene forms a secondary carbocation, and 2-methylpropene forms a tertiary carbocation. Since stability increases primary < secondary < tertiary, speed increases in this same order.
options.B: Incorrect. This puts 2-methylpropene (tertiary intermediate) as slowest, but a tertiary carbocation is actually the most stable and fastest. It confuses the order of stability.
options.C: Incorrect. This puts propene before ethene, suggesting a secondary carbocation is less stable than a primary one. In fact secondary > primary, so propene is faster than ethene.
options.D: Incorrect. This puts ethene as fastest and 2-methylpropene in the middle. Ethene gives only a primary carbocation, so it is the slowest, not the fastest.
